summary: A variable stores text under a name so you can reuse it. Environment variables like HOME and USER are set for you, and export passes your own variables to programs you start.
notes: wc -l < cs/roster.txt prints only the number. Without the <, wc also prints the file name.
bash -c '...' starts a new bash program. Single quotes keep $name from being filled in early, so the child shell reads it.
printenv lists every environment variable. PATH, HOME, and USER are the ones you will use most.
pitfall: name = Maya with spaces fails with name: command not found, because bash reads name as a command and = and Maya as its arguments. Write name=Maya with no spaces.
